artists.biography: Beth Gibbons (born 4 January 1965) is an English singer and songwriter best known as the singer and lyricist for the English band Portishead. With Adrian Utley, Gibbons and Barrow released the first Portishead album, Dummy, in 1994 and have produced two other studio albums, a live album, and various singles in the years since. She has also collaborated on a separate project with former Talk Talk bassist Paul Webb (Rustin Man). (Before she joined Geoff Barrow in Portishead, she auditioned for the singer's slot in .O.rang, the group formed by Webb after Talk Talk's late-Eighties departure from EMI, but Portishead's sudden success pre-empted matters.) In October 2002, they released the album Out of Season in the United Kingdom. The album peaked at number 28 in the UK Albums Chart. It was released in the United States a year later.

perplexity.description:
Lives Outgrown is the debut solo studio album by English singer Beth Gibbons, best known as the lead vocalist of Portishead. Released on May 17, 2024, through Domino Recording Company, the album marks a significant departure from Gibbons' trip-hop roots, embracing a blend of rock, folk, and classical influences. Over the course of a decade, Gibbons crafted ten introspective tracks that reflect on themes of aging, motherhood, loss, and the physical realities of life. The music is characterized by sparse arrangements, acoustic instrumentation, and Gibbons' signature emotive vocals, often accompanied by subtle percussion and atmospheric textures.

As Gibbons' first solo release, Lives Outgrown stands apart from her work with Portishead, offering a more personal and mature sound rooted in alternative folk and adult alternative pop/rock. The album was produced by Gibbons herself alongside James Ford and Lee Harris, and its lyrical depth and musical restraint have been widely praised. Critics have highlighted its emotional resonance and Gibbons' artistic growth, with the album receiving positive reviews and a nomination for the 2024 Mercury Prize. Commercially, it reached audiences through its release on Domino, solidifying Gibbons' reputation as a distinctive voice in contemporary rock and folk music.
